physical-development-lifespan.alt: Four columns along a lifespan arrow. Before birth: teratogens such as alcohol, nicotine, some drugs and infections can cross the placenta and harm the baby. Infancy and childhood: reflexes at birth (rooting, sucking, grasping) and motor milestones in a set order (sit, crawl, stand, walk at about 12 months, with a wide range). Adolescence: puberty, with primary and secondary sex characteristics, menarche and spermarche; the brain keeps maturing. Adulthood: strength and speed peak in the mid-20s then slowly decline, vision and hearing fade, and menopause often comes around age 50. Maturation sets the order; experience and health shape the timing.
